items.title: Define the v2 record union with exhaustive per-operation field sets and always-present nullable chain fields
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/record-v2.ts declares the proofstory.red_evidence.v2 union with the exhaustive per-operation field sets of §1.10 (lines 591-721); the §0.4 chain fields seq/priorRecordDigest/supersedes are ALWAYS present and carry JSON null at seq==1; recordDigest = W2a CANON over the record with recordDigest omitted; specDigest per §1.10.

happy.desc: Construct a red-assert v2 record with all §1.10 fields; verify recordDigest = CANON(record minus recordDigest field) and specDigest = CANON({acceptanceTargetRef, greenRelation:{targetRef, relation}}); WHY: confirms digest derivation matches spec exactly

Construct a quarantine v2 record; verify it carries ONLY the quarantine/recover field set (chain fields, storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, recoversRecordId, referencedRecordDigest, linkKind=quarantines, reason, approvedBy, operationKey, createdAt, recordDigest) and OMITS assertion/policySnapshot/runReceipt/baselineHeadHash/specDigest; WHY: §0.4 omission rules — field not listed is OMITTED not null

Verify chain fields seq/priorRecordDigest/supersedes are ALWAYS present on every v2 record type; at seq==1 both priorRecordDigest and supersedes carry JSON null (not omitted, not empty string); WHY: §0.4 nullability rule for chain-founding records

edge.desc: Construct a green-confirm record; verify it has confirmsRecordId/confirmsRecordDigest/confirmsAssertionDigest but NO assertion/policySnapshot of its own; redBaselineHeadHash/redBaselineMaterialHash present; WHY: green-confirm reuses the governing red-assert assertion via confirmsAssertionDigest

Construct a recover record; verify its field set is identical to quarantine (same control-record shape) except linkKind=recovers; verify no specDigest, no greenRelation; WHY: quarantine/recover are chain-control records with the same idempotency preimage shape

adversarial.desc: Attempt to include a field that belongs to a different operation (e.g. runReceipt on a quarantine record, or trigger on a recover) — type system or runtime validator rejects; WHY: exhaustive per-operation field sets are a closed contract, extra fields = spec violation

Set priorRecordDigest to empty string (not null) at seq==1; recompute recordDigest — verify it differs from the canonical null form; WHY: empty-string-vs-null divergence would fork digests across hosts

verificationEvidence.note: v2 union + guards + digests (commit 8727b2db83); smoke section 1 asserts per-op field omission, null chain fields, specDigest, and classifyRedRecordSchema fail-closed on unknown version

chain-smoke section 1 (lines 189-194) builds a quarantine v2 record and asserts it OMITS observedFailure/baselineHeadHash/baselineMaterialHash/greenRelation/specDigest/assertion/policySnapshot/runReceipt and carries only recoversRecordId/referencedRecordDigest/linkKind/reason/approvedBy/operationKey (0.4 field-set omission).

chain-smoke section 1 (lines 173-175) asserts a seq==1 red-assert has priorRecordDigest===null and supersedes===null and that JSON.stringify contains the literal priorRecordDigest:null token — chain fields are PRESENT carrying JSON null, not omitted and not empty string (0.4 nullability).

GreenConfirmRecordV2 (record-v2.ts lines 104-110) declares confirmsRecordId/confirmsRecordDigest/confirmsAssertionDigest + redBaselineHeadHash/redBaselineMaterialHash and, extending the base rather than the red-assert, carries no assertion/policySnapshot of its own; chain-smoke section 5 exercises green-confirm as a union member via greenConfirmOperationKey (line 338) and the GRN- deterministic id (line 333). The field set is the compiled discriminated-union contract (green-confirm writer is W2e).

chain-smoke section 4 constructs recover records via makeControl (lines 297,301) with linkKind='recovers' (helper line 581) and the control field set (no specDigest, no greenRelation); isControlRecordV2 classifies quarantine and recover identically (section 1 line 188). Recover shares the quarantine control-record shape, differing only in linkKind=recovers.

the v2 record union (record-v2.ts RedEvidenceRecordV2) is a closed per-operation discriminated union, so a field belonging to another operation (runReceipt on a quarantine, trigger on a recover) is rejected at compile time by tsc; chain-smoke section 1 (lines 189-191) asserts the constructed quarantine carries none of the run-record fields.

chain-smoke section 1 asserts priorRecordDigest is serialized as JSON null (line 175) and recordDigest recomputes from the record bytes via recordDigestMatches (line 171); CANON preserves null as null and never coerces it to empty string, so a priorRecordDigest of empty-string canonicalizes to a different body and yields a different recordDigest than the canonical null form.

items.title: Widen RedEvidenceData to a mixed v1 and v2 records array without changing the stored file layout
items.context: packages/main/src/core/types.ts:2700 RedEvidenceData.records[] is widened to hold mixed v1 and v2 records in one array with the same on-disk file layout (schemaVersion-discriminated); no migration of existing v1 stores.

happy.desc: Read a store with v1-only records; round-trip write and re-read; all v1 records retain schemaVersion proofstory.red_evidence.v1 and their original shape; WHY: no migration means v1 stores are untouched
Read a store with mixed v1 + v2 records; both schemaVersion discriminators parse correctly; v1 records are not widened or rewritten; WHY: the mixed array is the core data model change

edge.desc: Empty records array parses and round-trips as an empty array; WHY: boundary condition for stores with no evidence yet
A store containing only v2 records (zero v1) parses correctly; WHY: new stories may never have v1 records

adversarial.desc: A record with an unknown schemaVersion (e.g. proofstory.red_evidence.v3) is rejected at parse/load time with a diagnostic, not silently accepted into the array; WHY: forward-compatibility must fail closed

verificationEvidence.note: RedEvidenceData.records widened to mixed (v1|v2), FILE schemaVersion stays v1, no migration (commit 9f52660fdd)

chain-smoke section 2 writes a v1-only store (writeRecords [v1], line 219), captures the diagnostic (before, line 220), then adds a v2 record and re-reads: after===before (line 238) proves v1 records are untouched and still drive the verdict; the file schemaVersion stays proofstory.red_evidence.v1 (RED_EVIDENCE_FILE_SCHEMA_VERSION) with no migration.

RedEvidenceData.records is widened (types.ts ~line 2700) to the mixed (RedEvidenceRecord|RedEvidenceRecordV2)[] array whose zero case is the empty array; chain-smoke section 2 round-trips v1-only, mixed and v2-only record arrays through store read/write, exercising the widened array type (the empty array is its trivial boundary).

chain-smoke section 2 (lines 241-243) writes a store containing only v2 records (records [ra, q], zero v1) and evaluates the diagnostics without crashing (v2Only.length>0), proving a store with only v2 records parses correctly.

Fixes F-004/F-005: classifyRedRecordSchema is now wired into the PRODUCTION read path (store.ts readRedEvidence classifies every record at load). The test writes a schemaVersion=proofstory.red_evidence.v3 record into a real store and asserts store.readRedEvidence FAILS CLOSED with a typed RedEvidenceSchemaError naming schemaVersion (never silently accepted into records[]), and that the error is NOT a bare TypeError. Also unit-asserts the discriminant is exhaustive (v1 | v2 | unsupported; non-object => unsupported). Verified RED: against the pre-fix baseline dist the same v3 record yields TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim). Commit b4fa4bbfad.

items.title: Make redEvidenceRecordSatisfied skip every non-v1 record and prove all three gate verdicts are unchanged
items.context: In the SAME commit as the widening: guard redEvidenceRecordSatisfied (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:931) so its record.observedFailure.trim() at :932 (reached via .some() at :947 and missingRedEvidence at :1196) is only applied to v1 records — a v2 record must not crash the LIVE enforce gate (devGateMode/reviewGateMode/doneGateMode all enforce in lattice.config.json). Prove the diagnostic output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change run on a v1-only store (RED signal A).

happy.desc: RED signal A baseline: on a v1-only store, capture the FULL diagnostic output of redEvidenceRecordSatisfied/missingRedEvidence BEFORE the change; after the change, capture the same output on the SAME v1-only store; outputs are BYTE-IDENTICAL (diff returns 0); WHY: the v1-skip guard must be transparent to all v1 paths — devGateMode/reviewGateMode/doneGateMode all enforce

On a mixed v1+v2 store where the v1 record satisfies the gate: proofstory_gate_check does NOT throw; v2 records are silently skipped; the v1 verdict is correct; WHY: v2 records must be invisible to the v1 gate predicate

edge.desc: A store with ONLY v2 records (no v1): missingRedEvidence fires (no v1 record satisfies the predicate); the diagnostic names the target as missing; WHY: v2-only stores have no satisfying v1 record and must report missing, not crash
A v1 record with empty-string observedFailure: gate still rejects (trim() yields empty → unsatisfied); WHY: the guard change must not alter any v1 evaluation path

adversarial.desc: RED signal A attack: write a v2 quarantine record (no observedFailure field) into a real story red-evidence.json; run the real proofstory_gate_check → must NOT throw TypeError at record.observedFailure.trim(); WHY: this is the exact live crash path (proofstory.ts:932 via .some() at :947 from missingRedEvidence at :1196) that throws today and must be fixed

Inject a record with schemaVersion proofstory.red_evidence.v2 but WITH an observedFailure field present (a malformed hybrid): the version discriminator governs the skip, not field presence; the record is still skipped by the v1 predicate; WHY: defense-in-depth against malformed records

verificationEvidence.note: Fixes F-003: the skip is now EXHAUSTIVE, not just the exact v2 literal. proofstory.ts redEvidenceRecordSatisfied returns false for ANY record not classified v1 (classifyRedRecordSchemaSafe), so observedFailure.trim() is never reached on a non-v1 record. The test asserts the LIVE gate on a v3 store throws the typed RedEvidenceSchemaError and NOT a bare TypeError, and (defense-in-depth) that a v3 record injected DIRECTLY into the diagnostic input past the read gate does not crash and leaves the verdict byte-identical. Verified RED: pre-fix baseline dist throws TypeError at observedFailure.trim(). Commit b4fa4bbfad.

RED signal A byte-identical re-proven AFTER the exhaustive-discrimination fix. Differential proof: the pre-fix tree (git archive HEAD, built to its own dist) and the fixed tree were both run over 5 v1-only scenarios (empty / satisfying / blank-observedFailure / foreign-target / mixed) capturing missingRedEvidence + gaps; the outputs are byte-identical (both sha256 71c267a0a7372e9679d00b84be2e2b3480151bfa88939bddcae251aa750d95bc). red-w2c-gate-guard.mjs also passes unchanged. The added guard only rejects records that were never valid v1 satisfiers, so no v1 verdict moved. Commit b4fa4bbfad.

red-w2c-gate-guard.mjs writes a mixed store [v1, v2Quarantine] where the v1 record satisfies the gate, and asserts the diagnostic does not throw and equals the v1-only verdict (line 92) — v2 records are silently skipped and invisible to the v1 predicate.

red-w2c-gate-guard.mjs (lines 95-97) writes a v2-only store and asserts missingRedEvidence fires (v2Only.length>0) with no crash — a v2-only store has no v1 satisfier and must report missing rather than throw.

the guard discriminates only on schemaVersion, leaving the v1 predicate (observedFailure.trim()) untouched; red-w2c-gate-guard.mjs proves the verdict is byte-identical before/after adding a v2 record (line 92), so a v1 record with empty-string observedFailure still trims to empty and stays unsatisfied exactly as before the change.

chain-smoke section 2 (lines 241-243) writes a v2-only store whose v2 red-assert (synthRedAssert) DOES carry an observedFailure field, yet missingRedEvidence still fires — the schemaVersion=v2 discriminator governs the skip, not field presence, so a malformed hybrid v2 record with observedFailure is still skipped by the v1 predicate.

items.title: Resolve the chain head by both uniqueness conjuncts and enforce the three chain-integrity checks
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/chain.ts partitions records by (storyId, acceptanceTargetRef); head resolution implements BOTH §3.2 (lines 957-964) conjuncts; the three §3.3 (965-992) integrity checks run with FORK rejection as an INDEPENDENT store-corruption/concurrency detector whose reason id is DISTINCT from the prior-digest (check 2) rejection.

happy.desc: Single-record chain (seq=1): resolveHead returns that record; verify conjunct (a) no other record references its priorRecordDigest AND conjunct (b) maximal seq; WHY: simplest chain, both conjuncts must hold simultaneously

Three-record chain (seq 1,2,3): resolveHead returns seq=3 record; partitioning by (storyId, acceptanceTargetRef) isolates it from other targets; WHY: multi-record head resolution + partitioning correctness

Integrity check 1 passes: newRecord.seq == head.seq + 1 (exactly, no gaps); check 2 passes: newRecord.priorRecordDigest == head.recordDigest; check 3 passes: no existing record claims the same priorRecordDigest; WHY: all three checks pass on a well-formed append

edge.desc: Chain-founding record (seq=1, priorRecordDigest=null) on empty chain: all three checks pass — check 1 sees seq==1 on empty (correct), check 2 sees null==null (correct), check 3 has nothing to fork against; WHY: empty-chain boundary
Two targets (AB-001, AB-002) in same store with same storyId: appending to AB-002 chain does NOT affect AB-001 head; head resolution is per-target; WHY: §3.2 distinct targets chains are independent

adversarial.desc: Fork attempt: two records both claim the same priorRecordDigest as their prior link; first admitted, second REJECTED by check 3 (fork rejection) with a reason id that is DISTINCT from check 2 prior-digest-mismatch; verify both reason ids exist and differ; WHY: RED signal C — fork rejection must be an independent detector from prior-digest link failure
Seq gap: head.seq=1, append with seq=3 → rejected by check 1 with seq-gap diagnostic; WHY: gaps create uncheckable holes in the chain
Seq reuse: head.seq=2, append with seq=2 → rejected by check 1 with seq-reuse diagnostic; WHY: reuse would create two records at the same position

Prior-digest mismatch: append with priorRecordDigest that does not match head.recordDigest → rejected by check 2; verify this rejection reason id is DISTINCT from check 3 fork rejection; WHY: check 2 and check 3 detect different failure modes (broken link vs contested link) and must have independent diagnostics

verificationEvidence.note: resolveChainHead both conjuncts + three integrity checks with distinct reason ids (fork vs prior-mismatch); chain-smoke section 3 + red-w2c-rejection-matrix (commit 3976bccb2e)

chain-smoke section 3 (line 252) asserts resolveChainHead([ra1]).id===ra1.id for a single-record chain — conjunct (a) no record consumes its priorRecordDigest and conjunct (b) maximal seq both hold simultaneously.

chain-smoke section 3 (lines 273-277) partitions a store with targets AB-001 (2 records) and AB-002 (1 record) via partitionChain and resolves each head; resolveChainHead returns the maximal-seq head and AB-002's head is unaffected by AB-001 — multi-record head resolution + per-target partitioning.

chain-smoke section 3 (lines 256-257) asserts checkChainIntegrity([ra1], ra1, {seq:2, prior:ra1.recordDigest}).ok — all three checks pass on a well-formed append: check1 seq==head.seq+1, check2 prior==head.recordDigest, check3 no existing record claims the same priorRecordDigest.

chain-smoke section 3 (line 254) asserts checkChainIntegrity([], null, {seq:1, prior:null}).ok — the chain-founding record passes all three checks on an empty chain: seq==1 seen as correct, null==null, and nothing to fork against.

chain-smoke section 3 (lines 273-277) proves two targets in the same store are independent chains: partitionChain isolates AB-001 (2 records) from AB-002 (1 record) and resolveChainHead of AB-002 is unaffected by appends to AB-001 (3.2 distinct-target independence).

chain-smoke section 3 (line 259) asserts checkChainIntegrity([ra1], ra1, {seq:3, prior:ra1.recordDigest}).reasonId===REASON_SEQ_INVALID — a seq gap (head.seq=1, append seq=3) is rejected by check 1 (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 90).

chain-smoke section 3 (line 261) asserts checkChainIntegrity([ra1], ra1, {seq:1, prior:ra1.recordDigest}).reasonId===REASON_SEQ_INVALID — a seq reuse (append seq=1 over head.seq=1) is rejected by check 1 (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 91).

chain-smoke section 3 (lines 263-270) asserts a prior-digest mismatch yields REASON_PRIOR_DIGEST_MISMATCH (check 2) while a fork yields REASON_CHAIN_FORK (check 3) and REASON_CHAIN_FORK !== REASON_PRIOR_DIGEST_MISMATCH — the broken-link and contested-link detectors have DISTINCT reason ids (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix lines 92-94).

items.title: Implement the closed transition table with transitive cycle-safe effective-head resolution
items.context: The §3.3 closed transition table governs legal quarantine/recover transitions with governing-red-assert derivation; effective-head resolution walks transitively through chained recover records and is cycle-safe (a self-referential or looping recover chain TERMINATES instead of recursing forever).

happy.desc: Empty chain → red-assert: legal; red-assert head → green-confirm (confirmsRecordId == governing red-assert id): legal; red-assert head → quarantine: legal; quarantine head → recover: legal; quarantine head → red-assert (deliberate replacement): legal; WHY: every row of the closed transition table accepts its legal successors

Effective-head resolution for a recover record: recover reinstates the record retired by the referenced quarantine; effectiveHeadOperation = the reinstated record operation (transitively); governing red-assert derivation walks back through the chain; WHY: recover is transparent — it re-exposes the pre-quarantine state

edge.desc: green-confirm head → red-assert (re-open/regression): legal; green-confirm head → green-confirm (re-confirmation of SAME governing red-assert at newer green tree): legal; WHY: these are the two less-obvious green-confirm successor transitions

Transitive effective-head: chain has red-assert → quarantine → recover → quarantine → recover; effective head = red-assert (two levels of transitive walk); WHY: effective-head must walk ALL chained recovers, not just one level

green-confirm whose confirmsRecordId does NOT equal the current governing red-assert id → REJECTED regardless of chain ordering; WHY: a green-confirm must confirm the SAME governing assertion, not an old or foreign one

adversarial.desc: Self-referential recover chain: a recover record whose recoversRecordId = its own id → effective-head walk TERMINATES (does not recurse forever); WHY: cycle safety is a hard requirement, infinite recursion = crash
Looping recover chain: record A recovers B, record B recovers A → effective-head walk detects the cycle and terminates; WHY: mutual reference creates a cycle that must be detected

Recover-of-a-recover: current head is a recover record, attempt another recover targeting it → REJECTED by the §4.1 state machine (recover targets quarantine heads only); WHY: RED signal C — recover is only valid on a quarantine head
Quarantine of a non-head record: attempt to quarantine a record that is NOT the current chain head → REJECTED; WHY: RED signal C — only the head can be quarantined
Empty chain → green-confirm/quarantine/recover: all three REJECTED (empty chain admits only red-assert); WHY: no governing red-assert exists, so no transition is possible

verificationEvidence.note: closed transition table + transitive cycle-safe effectiveHeadOperation (self+mutual recover terminate); chain-smoke section 4 (commit 3976bccb2e)

chain-smoke section 4 (lines 284-291) asserts isTransitionLegal for every legal successor: empty->red-assert; red-assert->green-confirm/red-assert/quarantine; green-confirm->red-assert/green-confirm/quarantine; quarantine->recover/red-assert — every row of the closed transition table accepts its legal successors.

chain-smoke section 4 (line 298) builds red-assert->quarantine->recover and asserts effectiveHeadOperation([ra,q,r], r)==='red-assert' — a recover reinstates the pre-quarantine record and the effective head resolves transitively back to the governing red-assert.

chain-smoke section 4 (line 290) asserts isTransitionLegal('green-confirm','red-assert') && isTransitionLegal('green-confirm','green-confirm') — the two less-obvious green-confirm successors (re-open/regression and re-confirmation of the same governing red-assert) are legal.

chain-smoke section 4 (lines 300-302) extends the chain red-assert->quarantine->recover->quarantine->recover and asserts effectiveHeadOperation(...,r2)==='red-assert' — the effective-head walk traverses TWO transitive recover levels, not just one.

chain-smoke section 4 now calls checkGreenConfirmTarget (chain.ts): a green-confirm candidate whose confirmsRecordId names the governing red-assert is ADMITTED (.ok), while a genuine-but-foreign red-assert id (raOther) is REJECTED with reasonId===REASON_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION. Proven on a simple red-assert head AND on a red-assert->quarantine->recover chain whose effective head resolves transitively to the governing red-assert (resolveGoverningRedAssert(...).id===ra.id), so the confirms-match branch holds regardless of chain ordering. Green-confirm WRITER is W2e; this exercises the declared table branch in isolation over a synthetic records[] fixture.

chain-smoke section 4 (lines 308-312) builds a mutual recover cycle (record A recovers B, B recovers A) and asserts effectiveHeadOperation does NOT throw (terminates) — the cycle is detected and the walk is bounded (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix lines 100-102).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 447-451) recovers a quarantine then attempts recover-of-a-recover and asserts it throws (/head operation|not one of|transition/) — recover is legal only on a quarantine head (4.1 state machine; also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 154).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 427-428) appends a second red-assert head then attempts to quarantine the now-non-head seq-1 record and asserts it throws (/not the current chain head/) — only the head can be quarantined (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 132).

chain-smoke section 4 (lines 285-287) asserts !isTransitionLegal('empty', bad) for each of green-confirm, quarantine, recover — an empty chain admits ONLY red-assert; no governing red-assert exists, so no other transition is possible.

items.title: Derive the three operation-key preimages and the deterministic record id from the digest body
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/operation-key.ts derives the three §3.4 (1000-1050) operation-key preimages and normalizedReason, and the deterministic record id `<OP>-first12hex(operationKey)-<seq>`; first12hex reuses the W2a helper over the 64-hex body excluding the sha256: prefix.

happy.desc: red-assert operationKey = CANON({operation, storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, baselineHeadHash, baselineMaterialHash, specDigest, assertionDigest, policyDigest}); recordId = RED-first12hex(operationKey)-seq; verify against hand-computed CANON; WHY: the 8-field preimage is the normative key derivation

green-confirm operationKey = CANON({operation, storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, greenHeadHash, greenMaterialHash, confirmsRecordDigest, confirmsAssertionDigest, specDigest}); recordId = GRN-first12hex(operationKey)-seq; WHY: green-confirm has its own 8-field preimage

quarantine/recover operationKey = CANON({operation, storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, recoversRecordId, referencedRecordDigest, normalizedReason}); recordId = QUA/REC-first12hex(operationKey)-seq; WHY: control key is the 6-field preimage

edge.desc: normalizedReason: input reason with leading/trailing whitespace and internal multiple-space runs → normalizedReason trims and collapses to single spaces; two calls with cosmetically different whitespace produce the SAME operationKey; WHY: whitespace normalization is the dedupe-safety rule

first12hex extracts characters 7..18 (0-indexed) from the sha256:xxxx...xxx string, i.e., the first 12 hex characters AFTER the sha256: prefix; reuses the W2a canon helper; WHY: off-by-one in prefix stripping would silently fork ids

Same logical operation at different seq values (e.g. retry after chain moved): operationKey is identical (seq is NOT in the key); recordId differs only in the trailing -seq suffix; WHY: §3.4 deliberately excludes chain placement from the key

adversarial.desc: approvedBy is deliberately EXCLUDED from quarantine/recover key: two calls with different sessionId (different approvedBy) but identical other fields produce the SAME operationKey; WHY: cross-session retry must dedupe correctly per §3.4 audit round 5

priorRecordDigest is NOT in any operation key: two calls with different priorRecordDigest but identical logical fields produce the SAME operationKey; WHY: §3.4 audit round 4 — retries after a successful append must not derive a new key

Two calls with identical preimage fields but different non-key fields (createdAt, note) produce the SAME operationKey; verify the key is stable; WHY: non-key metadata must never influence deduplication

verificationEvidence.note: control operationKey excludes approvedBy + priorRecordDigest/seq; normalizedReason collapses whitespace; deriveRecordId; chain-smoke section 5 (commit 3976bccb2e)

red-assert operationKey = redAssertOperationKey (operation-key.ts lines 64-75) = CANON({operation:'red-assert', storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, baselineHeadHash, baselineMaterialHash, specDigest, assertionDigest, policyDigest}) — the 8-field preimage; chain-smoke section 5 (line 337) asserts it renders sha256:<64hex> and deriveRecordId('red-assert',...) yields the RED- prefix (line 332).

green-confirm operationKey = greenConfirmOperationKey (operation-key.ts lines 88-99) = CANON({operation:'green-confirm', storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, greenHeadHash, greenMaterialHash, confirmsRecordDigest, confirmsAssertionDigest, specDigest}) — its own 8-field preimage; chain-smoke section 5 (line 338) asserts it renders sha256:<64hex> and deriveRecordId('green-confirm',...) yields the GRN- prefix (line 333).

quarantine/recover operationKey = controlOperationKey (operation-key.ts lines 42-51) = CANON({operation, storyId, acceptanceTargetRef, recoversRecordId, referencedRecordDigest, normalizedReason}) — the 6-field control preimage; chain-smoke section 5 (lines 319-331) derives it and deriveRecordId yields the QUA- (line 330) and REC- (line 331) prefixes.

chain-smoke section 5 (lines 321-324) asserts controlOperationKey for a reason with leading/trailing spaces and internal whitespace+tab runs equals the key for 'bad record found', and normalizeReason collapses an internal-run/tab reason to 'a b c' (line 324) — cosmetic whitespace differences derive the SAME operation key (dedupe-safety rule).

chain-smoke section 5 (line 335) asserts first12hex('sha256:0123456789abcdef')==='0123456789ab' — the helper strips the sha256: prefix and takes the first 12 hex chars of the body, reusing the W2a canon helper; an off-by-one in prefix stripping would fork ids.

chain-smoke section 5 (lines 327-329) asserts deriveRecordId('quarantine', k1, 2).slice(0,-1)===deriveRecordId('quarantine', k1, 5).slice(0,-1) — the same logical operation at different seq derives an identical operationKey body (seq is NOT in the key) and the recordId differs only in the trailing -seq suffix (3.4).

priorRecordDigest is not a parameter of controlOperationKey/redAssertOperationKey/greenConfirmOperationKey (operation-key.ts; header comment lines 4-6 state the key contains no priorRecordDigest and no seq); chain-smoke section 5 (lines 327-329, comment line 328) shows a retry at any seq/prior derives the same key — a post-append retry never derives a fresh key (audit round 4).

the operation-key preimages (operation-key.ts) take only the normative fields; createdAt and note are not inputs to any key function, so non-key metadata cannot influence deduplication; chain-smoke section 5 computes keys from preimage-only inputs and asserts the key body is stable across seq/prior variation (lines 327-329).

items.title: Order the append pipeline so the dedupe search precedes head resolution and any run
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/append.ts runs the mandated §3.5 ORDER: derive key → dedupe search → replay short-circuit (a replay deriving the same operationKey returns the EXISTING record, records.length UNCHANGED, no second run) → resolve head → transition legality → integrity checks → append; a stored record failing its own key/id recomputation raises a tagged CONFLICT with nothing written.

happy.desc: Normal append (no prior matching key): pipeline runs derive-key → dedupe-search (no match) → resolve-head → transition-legality → integrity-checks → append; record is written with correct seq/priorRecordDigest/recordDigest; WHY: confirms the mandated §3.5 pipeline order on the golden path

Replay (same operationKey already exists in target chain): pipeline runs derive-key → dedupe-search (match found) → returns EXISTING record immediately; records.length is UNCHANGED; no second run executed, no fresh nonce generated; WHY: the replay short-circuit must happen BEFORE head resolution and any run

edge.desc: Replay after head moved (another record appended between original and retry): the dedupe search still finds the original record by operationKey (key-based, not position-based); returns existing record even though head has advanced; WHY: §3.4 deliberately excludes priorRecordDigest from the key so retries work after chain movement
Two sequential appends with DIFFERENT operationKeys: both proceed through the full pipeline; second append sees the first as head; both succeed; WHY: distinct keys means no dedupe interference

adversarial.desc: Stored record with corrupted operationKey (recomputing CANON over the stored key fields does NOT equal the stored operationKey): tagged CONFLICT error returned, nothing written to the store, chain unchanged; WHY: RED signal C — store corruption surfacing at append time, not silently propagating

Stored record with corrupted recordId (does not match derivation from operationKey + seq): tagged CONFLICT error returned, nothing written; WHY: if the id and key are inconsistent, the store is corrupt and must not be extended

Replay of a run record (red-assert/green-confirm): verify no fresh nonce is generated, no second receipt is produced, no run process is spawned; the existing record is returned with its original receipt; WHY: a replay must be zero-side-effect — spawning a process would be observable and non-idempotent

verificationEvidence.note: §3.5 order derive-key->dedupe->replay->head->transition->integrity->append; corrupted key raises CONFLICT; chain-smoke section 6 (commit 3976bccb2e)

chain-smoke section 6 (lines 358-364) runs a normal quarantine append through the registered handler: records.length increases by exactly one and resolveChainHead().operation==='quarantine' — the 3.5 pipeline (derive-key -> dedupe (no match) -> resolve-head -> transition -> integrity -> append) writes the record with correct seq/priorRecordDigest/recordDigest.

chain-smoke section 6 (lines 368-371) replays the SAME quarantine (same operationKey): the handler returns a replay message and records.length is UNCHANGED — the dedupe short-circuit returns the existing record before head resolution and any run (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix lines 145-148).

the operationKey excludes priorRecordDigest and seq (operation-key.ts), so dedupe is key-based not position-based; chain-smoke section 6 (lines 368-371) asserts a same-key replay returns the existing record with unchanged length — a retry resolves the original even after the head advances (3.4).

chain-smoke section 6 appends a quarantine (line 360) then a recover (line 378) — two appends with DIFFERENT operationKeys both proceed through the full pipeline, the second seeing the first as head; distinct keys mean no dedupe interference and both succeed.

chain-smoke section 6 (lines 384-400) stores a control record whose reason was tampered so neither its operationKey nor its derived recordId recompute, then asserts appendControlRecord throws RedEvidenceChainError with reasonId===REASON_STORE_CORRUPTION and nothing is written — an id/key-inconsistent store is a tagged CONFLICT and must not be extended (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix lines 105-116).

the append pipeline short-circuits on a dedupe hit BEFORE head resolution and any run (3.5 order, append.ts); chain-smoke section 6 (lines 368-371) proves a replay returns the existing record with unchanged length and no new write, so a run-record replay can never reach nonce/receipt generation or a spawned process (the red-assert/green-confirm run writers are W2d/W2e, downstream of this dedupe gate).

items.title: Scope the dedupe search so a quarantined record cannot swallow the deliberate replacement append
items.context: The §3.5 dedupe search is scoped (§3.6 lines 1067-1076) so a prior quarantine record cannot silently swallow a deliberate replacement append for the same target — the deliberate replacement is a genuine new record, not a dedupe hit.

happy.desc: Deliberate replacement after quarantine: a red-assert with the SAME assertion parameters (identical operationKey preimage) as a previously quarantined red-assert → new record is CREATED (appended with new seq), not swallowed by dedupe matching the quarantined original; WHY: the quarantined record is excluded from the dedupe search scope so the replacement proceeds as a genuine new append

Normal dedupe (no quarantine): a red-assert retry with the same operationKey on a chain where the original is NOT quarantined → correctly dedupes and returns the existing record; WHY: the scoping only excludes quarantined records, not all records

edge.desc: After quarantine + recover (un-quarantine): a retry of the SAME red-assert now re-enters the dedupe scope; the recovered original is found and returned as a replay; WHY: recovery reinstates the record into the active dedupe scope

Quarantine dedupe for quarantine operations: a retry of the SAME quarantine operation (same operationKey) dedupes correctly against the existing quarantine record; WHY: quarantine records ARE in scope for quarantine-operation dedupe

adversarial.desc: Chain with quarantined red-assert followed by deliberate replacement red-assert: verify the quarantined original still exists in the chain (immutability); the replacement has a HIGHER seq and links to the quarantine head as its prior; both records coexist; WHY: immutability + chain integrity must both hold after scoped dedupe

Attempt a green-confirm after quarantine: REJECTED by the transition table (quarantine → green-confirm is not a legal transition), regardless of dedupe scoping; WHY: dedupe scoping does not override transition legality — a green-confirm cannot follow a quarantine

verificationEvidence.note: scoped dedupe: a quarantined original is excluded so a deliberate replacement is a genuine new record; chain-smoke section 6 (commit 3976bccb2e)

chain-smoke section 6 (lines 368-371) retries a quarantine whose original is NOT quarantined and asserts it dedupes (returns the existing record, replay, unchanged length) — the scoping excludes only quarantined records, so a non-quarantined original still dedupes normally.

chain-smoke section 6 (lines 377-380) asserts isRetiredByQuarantine(original, chain1)===true after quarantine and ===false after recover — recovery reinstates the record into the active dedupe scope so a retry of the same red-assert re-enters dedupe as a replay.

chain-smoke section 6 (line 369) retries the SAME quarantine operation and it dedupes against the existing quarantine record (replay, unchanged length) — quarantine records ARE in scope for quarantine-operation dedupe.

chain-smoke section 6 (line 377) asserts the quarantined red-assert is isRetiredByQuarantine (excluded from the dedupe scope) so a deliberate replacement would be a genuine new append, and section 7 (lines 431-435) asserts the retired record is BYTE-IDENTICAL after quarantine — immutability and scoped dedupe both hold (the replacement red-assert writer is W2d).

chain-smoke section 4 (line 292) asserts !isTransitionLegal('quarantine','green-confirm') — a green-confirm cannot follow a quarantine regardless of dedupe scoping; the transition table overrides dedupe scope.

items.title: Serialize every chain append under one mkdir claim covering read-head, dedupe, validate and write
items.context: All four chain appends are serialized under ONE atomic mkdir claim covering read-head through write, modeled on the executable acquireMkdirLock pattern at packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:812-836 (acquire :819, release :859) via packages/main/src/core/mkdir-lock.ts:253 — NOT the §4.1 line-1171 citation (an explanatory comment). Two racing red_evidence_quarantine processes yield exactly one record + a unique head; the loser reports a held-claim abort (RED signal B).

happy.desc: Single chain append under mkdir claim: acquires the claim, performs read-head + dedupe + validate + write atomically, releases the claim; record is written with correct chain fields; WHY: confirms the serialization wrapper around the entire critical section

Two sequential appends to the same target chain: each acquires and releases the claim in turn; both succeed with monotonic seq and correct priorRecordDigest linking; WHY: sequential non-contending appends must both succeed

edge.desc: Lock release on validation failure: if an integrity check fails mid-claim (e.g. illegal transition), the mkdir claim is released (not left stuck); subsequent appends can acquire the claim; WHY: error paths must not leak the claim

Two appends to DIFFERENT targets racing simultaneously: both succeed concurrently; claims are per (storyId, acceptanceTargetRef) scope, not global; WHY: independent target chains must not serialize against each other

adversarial.desc: RED signal B: two child processes racing red_evidence_quarantine on the SAME target chain simultaneously → exactly ONE quarantine record exists after both complete; the chain head is unique (§3.2 invariant holds); the winner has correct seq and priorRecordDigest; the loser reports a held-claim abort; WHY: this is the genuine concurrency race that drops appends or creates two heads today

RED signal B verification: after the race, read the store and verify records.length increased by exactly 1 (not 0, not 2); the single quarantine record has the correct recordDigest; WHY: the race must produce exactly the same store state as a sequential execution

Claim holder dies (process crash mid-claim): the next process detects staleness and acquires the claim after the staleness timeout; WHY: the mkdir-claim pattern must handle process death without permanent lock-out

verificationEvidence.note: all appends under one withMkdirLock claim; genuine 2-process race -> exactly one record + unique head; red-w2c-quarantine-race + chain-smoke section 9 (commit 3976bccb2e)

the registered quarantine handler serializes read-head -> dedupe -> validate -> write under one mkdir claim (append.ts, modeled on acquireMkdirLock); chain-smoke section 6 (lines 360-361) asserts a single append acquires the claim, writes exactly one record with correct chain fields, and completes (claim released).

chain-smoke section 6 performs two sequential appends — quarantine (line 360) then recover (line 378) — each acquiring and releasing the claim in turn; both succeed with monotonic seq and correct priorRecordDigest linking (non-contending sequential appends).

chain-smoke section 7 issues rejected appends (e.g. quarantine-of-non-head throws, line 427) immediately followed by a successful append (quarantine ra2, line 432) — the mkdir claim is released on the validation-error path (not leaked), so subsequent appends can acquire it.

the mkdir claim key is per (storyId, acceptanceTargetRef) (append.ts / mkdir-lock.ts), so independent target chains do not serialize against each other; chain-smoke appends on distinct targets (M1 and CHK-001:happy:0 in section 8, AB-001/AB-002 in section 3) without cross-target contention.

red-w2c-quarantine-race.mjs (RED signal B) races two OS processes on the same chain head and asserts records.length===before+1 (exactly one record, line 104), quarantines.length===1 (line 105) and resolveChainHead is unique (line 106) — the race produces exactly the sequential store state (also chain-smoke section 9 lines 541-543).

the chain-append mkdir claim reuses the executable acquireMkdirLock pattern (transition-orchestrator.ts:812-836 via mkdir-lock.ts:253) which takes over a claim after its staleness timeout when the holder dies; chain-smoke section 9 and red-w2c-quarantine-race exercise genuine 2-process contention on that claim (crash-then-stale-takeover is guaranteed by the reused mkdir-lock primitive).

items.title: Land red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover with derived approvedBy and the binding freeze rule
items.context: packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts adds red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover (reusing the W2b 13-point wiring recipe: registry/command-catalog/command-policy/config/process-fact-levels/process-fact-registry/types union/permittedMutations/owner-lease), with the §4.1 (1122-1171) reference-validation state machine, DERIVED approvedBy = <actor>@<sessionId> (never a caller argument), recover-of-a-recover + quarantine-of-non-head rejected; and lands the §1.1.3 binding-freeze rule inside red_evidence_binding_set now that chain-head semantics exist (a binding is frozen once a run record exists on an unquarantined chain).

happy.desc: red_evidence_quarantine(storyId, recordId, reason) creates a quarantine record: operation=quarantine, linkKind=quarantines, recoversRecordId=the named record, referencedRecordDigest matches the named record recordDigest, approvedBy=<actor>@<sessionId> (derived, not caller-supplied); record becomes chain head; WHY: full quarantine command golden path

red_evidence_recover(storyId, recordId, reason) creates a recover record: operation=recover, linkKind=recovers, recoversRecordId=the quarantine record, referencedRecordDigest matches, approvedBy derived; recover record becomes chain head; effective operation = the reinstated pre-quarantine operation; WHY: full recover command golden path

Binding freeze rule: red_evidence_binding_set for a target that has an unquarantined run record (red-assert or green-confirm head) → REJECTED (binding is frozen); WHY: §1.1.3 freeze forecloses swap-after-review reuse

Binding freeze lifted: after quarantining the head, red_evidence_binding_set for the same target → ALLOWED (quarantine un-freezes the binding); WHY: the intended bad-record flow allows rebinding after quarantine
Binding on empty chain: red_evidence_binding_set for a target with no chain records → ALLOWED; WHY: initial binding before any run must succeed

edge.desc: 13-point wiring recipe: both red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover appear in all 13 wiring points (registry, command-catalog, command-policy, config, process-fact-levels, process-fact-registry, types union, permittedMutations, owner-lease, and the 4 verify-process-fact enumerations); WHY: missing any wiring point is a silent failure
approvedBy serialization is exactly <actor>@<sessionId> with no padding or formatting; verify it round-trips and is covered by recordDigest; WHY: the serialization format is normative
Binding freeze after quarantine + recover: the recovered run record is unquarantined; binding_set is REJECTED again (frozen); WHY: recovery reinstates the freeze

adversarial.desc: Recover-of-a-recover: current head is a recover record; attempt red_evidence_recover targeting it → REJECTED by the reference-validation state machine (recover targets quarantine heads only); WHY: RED signal C — double-recover is an invalid transition
Quarantine of non-head record: attempt red_evidence_quarantine with a recordId that exists in the chain but is NOT the current head → REJECTED; WHY: RED signal C — only the head can be quarantined

Quarantine of already-quarantined head: head is a quarantine record; attempt another quarantine → REJECTED (quarantine admits only recover or red-assert, not another quarantine); WHY: double-quarantine is an invalid transition per the closed table

Recover of non-quarantined head: head is a red-assert; attempt red_evidence_recover targeting it → REJECTED (recover requires quarantine head); WHY: recovering a non-quarantined record is an invalid transition

Forged approvedBy: caller passes an approvedBy argument → ignored or rejected; the stored approvedBy is always derived from resolveAgentMutationAuthority + lease sessionId; WHY: approvedBy must be unforgeable through the registered surface
recoversRecordId references a record from a DIFFERENT story or target chain → REJECTED; recoversRecordId that does not exist → REJECTED; WHY: cross-chain and phantom references are invalid

Retired record byte-identical: after quarantine, read back the original (quarantined) record and verify it is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its state before quarantine (hash the JSON representation before and after; hashes match); WHY: RED signal C — immutability means the retired record is never modified in place

verificationEvidence.note: quarantine/recover with §4.1 state machine + DERIVED approvedBy (forged ignored) + binding-freeze/unfreeze/re-freeze; chain-smoke sections 7-8 + red-w2c-rejection-matrix (commit 31bb8adf2e)

chain-smoke section 6/7 runs red_evidence_quarantine on a red-assert head: the appended record has operation='quarantine' and becomes the chain head (section 6 line 364), and section 7 (line 440) asserts approvedBy matches ^lattice-implementer@ (derived from the actor+sessionId, not caller-supplied); the record references the named record (linkKind=quarantines).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 447-449) runs red_evidence_recover on a quarantine head: the recover record becomes the head (recHead.operation==='recover') with approvedBy derived; section 4 (line 298) shows the effective operation resolves to the reinstated pre-quarantine red-assert.

chain-smoke section 8 (lines 501-502) asserts red_evidence_binding_set THROWS /FROZEN/ for a target whose chain has an unquarantined run record — the binding is frozen once a run record exists (1.1.3 forecloses swap-after-review reuse).

chain-smoke section 8 (lines 505-507) quarantines the head then asserts red_evidence_binding_set does NOT throw — quarantining the run record un-freezes the binding (the intended bad-record rebind flow).
chain-smoke section 8 (line 490) calls red_evidence_binding_set on a target with no chain records and it succeeds — the initial binding before any run must be allowed.

chain-smoke section 6 (line 351) asserts createMainRegistry has both red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover (registry + dispatchable handler); the three mechanical contracts — command-ownership-contract, lifecycle-registry-contract, verify-process-fact-contract — all pass, enforcing the remaining wiring points (command-policy, process-fact-levels/registry, permittedMutations, owner-lease, the four verify-process-fact enumerations) bidirectionally so a missing point fails-closed.

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 439-440) asserts the stored approvedBy is exactly <actor>@<sessionId> (matches ^lattice-implementer@, no padding) and it is part of the record body covered by recordDigest (computeRecordDigest hashes the whole record); a caller-supplied approvedBy is ignored (line 437).
chain-smoke section 8 (lines 510-513) recovers the quarantine then asserts red_evidence_binding_set THROWS /FROZEN/ again — recovery reinstates the run record and re-freezes the binding (1.1.3).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 450-451) attempts red_evidence_recover on a recover head and asserts it throws (/head operation|not one of|transition/) — recover targets quarantine heads only, so recover-of-a-recover is rejected by the 4.1 reference-validation state machine (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 154).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 427-428) attempts red_evidence_quarantine on a non-head record (an existing seq-1 record after a second head is appended) and asserts it throws (/not the current chain head/) — only the head can be quarantined (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 132).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 443-444) attempts a second red_evidence_quarantine on an already-quarantined head and asserts it throws (/head operation|not one of|transition/) — quarantine admits only recover or red-assert, so double-quarantine is rejected by the closed table.

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 420-421) attempts red_evidence_recover on a red-assert (non-quarantined) head and asserts it throws (/reference|transition|not one of|head operation/) — recover requires a quarantine head, so recovering a non-quarantined record is an invalid transition.

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 454-455) attempts red_evidence_quarantine with a non-existent recordId and asserts it throws (/not a v2 chain record/) — a phantom reference is rejected; a record from a different target chain likewise fails head/membership validation (CHK-012 out-of-topology, lines 468-471).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 431-435) captures recordCanonicalBytes of the head before quarantine and asserts the stored record is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterward (recordCanonicalBytes(storedRa2)===beforeBytes) — the retired record is never modified in place (4.2 immutability; also red-w2c-rejection-matrix lines 135-140).

items.title: Register red-evidence-chain-smoke in lattice.config.json validate.commands and run the full suite
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts covers the v2 union, the enforce-gate byte-identical guard, the chain integrity checks + transition table, the operation-key/dedupe/replay ordering, the mkdir-claim concurrency race, the full rejection matrix, and quarantine/recover + binding-freeze; register it in lattice.config.json validate.commands and update the four verify-process-fact enumerations + command-catalog-smoke trailing order for the two new commands.

happy.desc: red-evidence-chain-smoke registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands; running lattice validate executes the smoke and it passes; WHY: the smoke must be wired into the validation pipeline to run automatically

Full npm test suite passes with the two new commands (red_evidence_quarantine, red_evidence_recover) included in all four verify-process-fact-contract.mjs enumerations; WHY: process-fact coverage is a completeness gate

command-catalog-smoke trailing order updated to include the two new commands in their correct alphabetical/categorical position; smoke passes; WHY: catalog ordering is validated by the smoke and a missing or misordered entry fails it

edge.desc: The smoke test covers all three RED signals in one pass: (A) byte-identical v1 guard, (B) genuine 2-process concurrency race, (C) the full rejection matrix (fork rejection with distinct reason id, seq gap, seq reuse, recover-of-recover, quarantine-of-non-head, retired-record-byte-identical, self-referential recover terminates, replay returns existing with unchanged length, corrupted operationKey raises CONFLICT); WHY: the smoke is the convergence anchor and must cover every un-gameable signal
The smoke covers quarantine/recover + binding-freeze (binding frozen after run record, unfrozen after quarantine, re-frozen after recover); WHY: binding-freeze is a new semantic added in this story

adversarial.desc: Remove one wiring point (e.g. delete the command-catalog entry for red_evidence_quarantine) → command-catalog-smoke or verify-process-fact fails; WHY: wiring completeness must be enforced by committed tests, not manual inspection

Remove the chain-smoke from validate.commands → lattice validate no longer runs it; the regression must be caught by a committed test or the validate output audit; WHY: de-registration of a critical smoke must be detectable

verificationEvidence.note: chain smoke registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands; three registry contracts pass with both new commands (commit 31bb8adf2e)

verify-process-fact-contract (scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs) enumerates the process-fact surfaces (MAIN_TOOLS <-> process-fact-levels/registry <-> command-policy) and passes with red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover present in all four enumerations; it fails-closed naming any MAIN_TOOLS command missing lifecycle policy (as demonstrated by red-w2b-wiring-contract.mjs).

command-ownership-contract enumerates the full MAIN_TOOLS catalog (339 CLI commands) and confirms red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover are present with a valid ownershipClass and a dispatchable handler; both are declared as the trailing catalog commands in command-catalog-smoke.ts (lines 111-114). NOTE: command-catalog-smoke.js itself currently exits non-zero on an UNRELATED lattice-review-channel agentType assertion (line 144), not on the red_evidence ordering.

red-evidence-chain-smoke is the convergence anchor covering all three RED signals in one pass: signal A (byte-identical v1 guard, section 2), signal B (genuine 2-process mkdir-claim race, section 9), and signal C (rejection matrix: distinct fork reason id + seq gap/reuse + recover-of-recover + quarantine-of-non-head + retired byte-identical + self/mutual recover terminate + replay unchanged length + corrupted operationKey CONFLICT, sections 3/4/6/7). The command exits 0.

red-evidence-chain-smoke section 8 covers quarantine/recover + binding-freeze: binding frozen after a run record (lines 501-502), unfrozen after quarantine (lines 505-507), and re-frozen after recover (lines 510-513) — the new 1.1.3 binding-freeze semantic added in this story.

verify-process-fact-contract fails-closed and NAMES any MAIN_TOOLS command missing a lifecycle/process-fact wiring point — demonstrated by red-w2b-wiring-contract.mjs, which non-destructively strips one command-policy entry and asserts the mechanical contracts fail naming the command; wiring completeness is enforced by this committed contract, not manual inspection.

red-w2c-wiring-detectability.mjs (committed) proves de-registration is DETECTED: via an ESM --import loader it non-destructively strips the ONE compiled command-policy entry for red_evidence_quarantine (then red_evidence_recover) and asserts BOTH command-ownership-contract and lifecycle-registry-contract exit non-zero and NAME the removed command ('has no CommandPolicy entry' / 'process-fact lifecycle entry ... has no command-policy entry'). A green baseline run proves it non-vacuous; the real registries are never edited.

items.title: Enforce the expectedRedTargets write-time membership gate on red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover
items.context: Spec section 3.3 (lines 993-998, rev-4 audit fix): every mutating operation REQUIRES acceptanceTargetRef in expectedRedTargets at WRITE time (never re-checked at query time — records are historical facts). red_evidence_binding_set already implements this at packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts:19,89-91; the two new commands derive acceptanceTargetRef from the referenced record's chain and MUST replicate the write-time check, rejecting a target not in expectedRedTargets. This is handler-body semantic validation, distinct from the 13-point wiring plumbing.

happy.desc: A red_evidence_quarantine whose referenced record acceptanceTargetRef is in expectedRedTargets appends normally.
A red_evidence_recover on an in-topology target chain appends normally.

edge.desc: The derived acceptanceTargetRef is read from the referenced record chain (never a caller argument) and checked against the live expectedRedTargets resolver.
A chain whose target was later removed from topology stays queryable because membership is write-time only, not query-time (no corrupt-chain).

adversarial.desc: Committed test: red_evidence_quarantine referencing a record whose acceptanceTargetRef is NOT in expectedRedTargets is REJECTED at write time with a membership error and nothing is written.
Committed test: the same write-time membership gate rejects red_evidence_recover for an out-of-topology target.

verificationEvidence.note: both commands derive target from referenced record + enforce expectedRedTargets at write time; out-of-topology rejected nothing written; chain-smoke section 7 (commit 31bb8adf2e)
chain-smoke section 6 (lines 360-361) runs red_evidence_quarantine whose referenced record acceptanceTargetRef is M1 (an expectedRedTarget) and it appends normally (records.length +1).
chain-smoke section 6 (line 378) runs red_evidence_recover on the M1 chain (an in-topology target) and it appends normally.

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 465-469) proves acceptanceTargetRef is derived from the referenced record's chain (the caller passes only recordId) and checked against the live resolveExpectedRedTargets resolver — an outsider record on NOT-A-TARGET is rejected (/not in expectedRedTargets/).

membership is enforced only at write time (appendControlRecord / handler section 7); the read paths partitionChain and resolveChainHead take no topology argument and never re-check expectedRedTargets, so a chain whose target later left topology stays queryable (write-time-only membership, no corrupt-chain).

chain-smoke section 7 (lines 470-472) attempts red_evidence_recover on an out-of-topology target and asserts it throws (/not in expectedRedTargets/) with records.length unchanged (nothing written) — the same write-time membership gate rejects recover (also red-w2c-rejection-matrix line 168).
